views.Timeline: PlotWeave / Carmilla Ch.17 · Italy and After Ctrl+K Dashboard Timeline Characters Maps MORE Calendar Items Relations Arc Lore Factions Knowledge Settings Pin open 1× Ch.17 · Conclusion Italy and After 1 · Prologue 2 · An Early Fright 3 · A Guest 4 · We Compare Notes 5 · Her Habits—A Saunter 6 · A Wonderful Likeness 7 · A Very Strange Agony 8 · Descending 9 · Search 10 · The Doctor 11 · Bereaved 12 · The Story 13 · A Petition 14 · The Woodman 15 · The Meeting 16 · Ordeal and Execution 17 · Conclusion Laura’s Narrative (17 chapters) Narrative Chronological Ch. 1 — Prologue — An editor introduces Doctor Hesselius’s papers and the careful testimony of a woman who has since died. 1 scene · 213 words Read to here Ch. 2 — An Early Fright — Laura describes her Styrian home, household, and the ruined Karnstein estate nearby. Six-year-old Laura wakes beside a beautiful stranger and feels two sharp punctures at her breast. A doctor, Laura’s father, and an elderly priest try to settle the terrified child after the apparition. 3 scenes · 1,719 words Read to here Ch. 3 — A Guest — A summer walk is darkened by news that the General’s ward has died after a mysterious illness. Laura’s household lingers outside while unease gathers beneath a peaceful summer evening. A noblewoman’s carriage crashes before the schloss, leaving her daughter stunned on the road. Laura persuades her father to shelter the injured traveler while the girl’s mother continues an urgent journey. 4 scenes · 2,583 words Read to here Ch. 4 — We Compare Notes — The household carries its unexpected guest across the drawbridge and prepares a room for her. The household compares troubling impressions of the carriage party and the secrecy demanded by its lady. After the physician departs, Laura recognizes the guest as the woman from her childhood terror. Carmilla claims that she too dreamed of Laura twelve years earlier, and their mutual alarm becomes intimacy. Laura finds her guest beautiful and charming in daylight despite a residue of unease. 5 scenes · 2,506 words Read to here Ch. 5 — Her Habits—A Saunter — Carmilla offers only her name, noble birth, and western home while refusing every useful detail. Carmilla’s passionate embraces leave Laura divided between attraction, embarrassment, and dread. A village funeral hymn provokes Carmilla’s anger and a sudden seizure beneath the trees. A traveling mountebank sells protections against the oupire and notices Carmilla’s pointed tooth. Laura’s father and the doctor discuss spreading deaths while Carmilla rejects prayerful explanations. 5 scenes · 3,531 words Read to here Ch. 6 — A Wonderful Likeness — Newly cleaned family pictures are unpacked in the great hall. A portrait dated 1698 bears Carmilla’s exact likeness and the name of Countess Mircalla Karnstein. On the drawbridge Carmilla’s declaration of love intensifies into language of possession and death. Carmilla recovers from a strange lapse and dismisses Laura’s concern about the local sickness. 4 scenes · 1,301 words Read to here Ch. 7 — A Very Strange Agony — Laura’s father asks how Carmilla’s mother can be reached, but the guest remains bound to secrecy. Preparing for bed, Carmilla speaks of vows, sacrifice, and an old illness she remembers like drowning. Alarmed by deaths in the district, Laura locks her door and keeps a light burning beside her. Laura dreams awake as a catlike shape crosses her bed, strikes her breast, and becomes a woman at the door. 4 scenes · 1,484 words Read to here Ch. 8 — Descending — Laura conceals the night’s terror and hears that a woman has been seen walking below Carmilla’s window. Carmilla professes fear for Laura and attributes the frightening night to natural causes. Laura’s strength ebbs through recurring dreams and sensations while she refuses to admit that she is ill. A voice naming itself as Laura’s mother warns her of an assassin and a light reveals Carmilla at her bed. Laura and the household find Carmilla’s locked bedroom silent and apparently empty. 5 scenes · 1,926 words Read to here Ch. 9 — Search — A search of the sealed chamber and the entire schloss produces no trace of Carmilla. At one o’clock Laura finds Carmilla sitting calmly in the room that had been searched. Laura’s father proposes that Carmilla unlocked the door in her sleep and later returned unseen. 3 scenes · 1,209 words Read to here Ch. 10 — The Doctor — A servant is posted outside Carmilla’s room before the doctor comes to examine Laura. The doctor makes Laura expose a small discolored spot below her throat and privately alarms her father. The doctor orders constant companionship for Laura and arranges to inspect Carmilla that evening. A delayed letter from General Spielsdorf sends Laura, her father, and Madame Perrodon toward Karnstein.
